headline: Relief rally inside a bigger downtrend: 4H flipped bullish, Daily and Weekly still bearish
summary: Gold bounced hard from the 4,084 two-month low and broke 4H structure (bullish CHoCH above 4,152), completing an inverse head and shoulders. But price is now pushing into the daily bearish FVG (4,194–4,252) while the Weekly and Daily trends are still down, so treat this as a counter-trend rally until a daily candle closes above 4,230.

setup.invalidation: Short idea fails on a daily close above 4,230. Long idea fails on a 1H close below 4,170.

analysis.body:
The weekly trend is bearish. A BOS at 4,141 in June confirmed it, and every rally since the 5,600 February top has made a lower high (4,873, then 4,689). Price now sits in the lower 22% of the 3,945–4,873 weekly range, inside a weekly bullish FVG (4,113–4,308). That is where buyers stepped in at 4,084, so the weekly picture is bearish but at a level where bounces are normal.

The daily is also bearish: a BOS down at 4,122 on 7 October, with the 20, 50 and 200 EMAs stacked downward (4,228 / 4,280 / 4,315). Friday's rally broke a falling wedge upward but ran straight into the daily bearish FVG at 4,194–4,252. That FVG, the 20 EMA (4,228) and the daily internal high (4,230) form one resistance band.
analysis.title: Big picture: Weekly and Daily

analysis.body: The 4H flipped bullish on 9 October with a CHoCH above 4,152, completing an inverse head and shoulders with its head at 4,084. Its measured target (~4,184) has already been reached. Price is in the top 20% of the 4H range (4,111–4,206), which is premium: a poor place to start new longs. The 4H 200 EMA at 4,263 sits just above the daily FVG, so 4,230–4,263 is a heavy ceiling.
analysis.title: Intermediate: 4H

analysis.body: The 1H is bullish with a clean higher low at 4,170 and a bull flag forming under the 4,206 high, and the 15M has a bullish EMA stack. Short-term momentum favours one more push toward 4,206–4,252. The key line is 4,170: while it holds, dips are being bought; a 1H close below it would mean the relief rally is over and the daily downtrend is back in charge.
analysis.title: Execution: 1H and 15M

analysis.body: Weekly and Daily point down; 4H, 1H and 15M point up. The weighted score is −2 out of ±10, so the bias is mixed. This is a counter-trend rally into higher-timeframe supply: the daily bearish FVG, the 4H 200 EMA and the previous week high all sit between 4,194 and 4,263. The better-odds trade is a short from that zone once the lower timeframes turn back down. Longs only make sense after a daily close above 4,230 reclaims structure.
analysis.title: How the timeframes fit together

analysis.body: Spot gold rose about 0.9% on Friday, recovering from Wednesday's two-month low as the dollar eased and the 10-year Treasury yield fell for a second session. The bigger backdrop is still hawkish: the Fed hiked in September, and markets price roughly 18% odds of another hike in October and 82% by December, which tends to cap gold rallies. Middle East supply risk keeping oil high, plus steady central-bank buying, help cushion dips. The Fed meeting on 27–28 October is the next major catalyst.
analysis.title: Macro backdrop

analysis.body: Gold is closed until Monday's open (about 6 AM Malaysia time). PAXG has drifted between 4,186 and 4,190 over the weekend. Your broker's XAUUSD closed near 4,195, about $8 above PAXG, so adjust the levels here by roughly that amount on your MT5 chart. Watch for a Monday gap: a gap up into 4,206–4,230 would put price straight into the sell zone.

tfs.note: Lower highs since the 5,600 top (4,873 then 4,689). Price is in the lower half of the 3,945–4,873 range, sitting on a weekly bullish FVG (4,113–4,308) that buyers defended at 4,084.
Made a two-month low at 4,084, then Friday rallied to 4,206. Price is now inside the daily bearish FVG 4,194–4,252. A daily close above 4,230 is needed to flip the daily internal trend.
Structure flipped up on Friday. The inverse head and shoulders is confirmed and its ~4,184 target is already hit. The 4H stays bullish while 4,170 holds; the 4H 200 EMA at 4,263 is overhead.
Higher low at 4,170 and a bull flag under the 4,206 high. A break above 4,200–4,206 points to the flag target near 4,252, the top of the daily FVG.
Short-term trend is up. The 4,180–4,183 higher lows are the first sign of trouble if they break.
